reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational principle of C3-ensemble-cept is to combine heterogeneous expert models using learned Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA) weights instead of naive product aggregation. This ensures compatibility among incompatible models by conditioning their contributions on shared latent structures. The conditional ensemble prediction primitive formalizes this as a weighted sum over modalities, where weights are derived from likelihoods. The dynamic state layer introduces a hidden Markov process to model streakiness or momentum, allowing confidence to adapt in real time. These two primitives together enable robust, adaptive ensemble behavior under uncertainty. Failure modes include overfitting to rare events or misalignment between expert models. The modality-weighted ensemble primitive ensures that injury-related signals do not dominate but instead act as a confidence downgrade, preserving model integrity. The interplay between these operators creates a dual structure: one for static expert combination and another for dynamic adjustment.
